statement: Running `orders total` prints nothing; the total is silently swallowed.
`orders list --search NAME` always lists every order, ignoring the search term.
Searching by customer name like "Alice" returns no results because the search actually matches the item field.
Searching "alice" (lowercase) finds nothing because the search is now case-sensitive.
`orders total` undercounts by leaving out the last order in the list.
`orders list` never shows the first matching order.
`orders list` reorders rows by price instead of showing them in the original order.
Passing `--search NAME` is accepted but the name is thrown away, so results are never filtered.
The CLI ships a stale, shorter snapshot of the order list baked in at build time; new orders added to the data module never show up in `orders list`.
`orders total` always prints "Total: 880.00" no matter which orders are shown.

category: works in dev but not on the production build
statement: In a production build (NODE_ENV=production) the total loses its cents formatting, e.g. "Total: 880" instead of "Total: 880.00".
Running an invalid command like `orders foo` prints the usage error but exits successfully (status 0) instead of failing.
`orders total` adds up order IDs instead of order totals, producing a nonsense grand total.
`orders list` prints the item name in the customer column and the customer name in the item column.
`orders total` crashes with a stack trace instead of printing a total, for any search (including no search at all).
Searching for a customer with no orders shows a blank list instead of "No orders match ...".
Typing a customer's name into search returns nothing; search actually matches against the numeric order ID.
Installing the CLI (npm link/npm i -g) points the `orders` command at dist/orders.mjs, a build output that was never generated, so the installed command can't be found.
Every total is off by one cent too high.
Search results for a customer with multiple orders show them in reverse order instead of original order.
`orders list` never shows more than the first two orders, even when more match.
A search query with a trailing space (e.g. "Alice ") matches nothing even though "Alice" would.
`orders list` crashes with a TypeError instead of printing any rows.
`orders total --search NAME` reports the grand total of every order, not just the ones matching the search.
Searching "alice" in lowercase finds nothing because the stored customer name "Alice Nguyen" is compared without lowercasing it.
Running `orders list` prints just the total, and `orders total` prints the row listing; the two commands are swapped.
`orders list` prints the last matching order twice.
Every total is inflated by 10% above the sum of the listed orders.
`orders list --search Alice` fails with a usage error; the flag-detection logic checks the arguments in the wrong order.
`orders list` reorders rows alphabetically by customer name instead of showing them in original order.
Searching for any missing customer shows the fixed message "No orders match Nobody" instead of naming the actual query.
The CLI fails to start at all: `orders list` and `orders total` both crash immediately with a module load error.
